module_title: Superlatives - Man-Made Infrastructure, Extreme Points, and Topography
introduction: Designed for UPSC, State PCS, and SSC CGL Tier-2, this advanced tier targets extreme oceanic depths, landlocked nations, and India's rapidly updating man-made infrastructure, such as the longest bridges, tunnels, and highest-altitude polling stations.

core_concepts.title: Global Extreme Depths
core_concepts.description: The deepest oceanic trench in the world is the Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean. Its deepest point is known as the Challenger Deep (approx. 10,984 meters).

core_concepts.title: Landlocked Extremes
core_concepts.description: The largest landlocked country (a country entirely enclosed by land with no access to the open ocean) in the world is Kazakhstan. The smallest republic in the world is the island nation of Nauru.

core_concepts.title: India's Longest Bridges and Tunnels
core_concepts.description: India's longest river bridge is the Bhupen Hazarika Setu (Dhola-Sadiya Bridge - 9.15 km) over the Lohit River. The longest highway tunnel above 10,000 feet is the Atal Tunnel (Rohtang - 9.02 km). The longest railway tunnel is the Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel (J&K).

core_concepts.title: High-Altitude Records
core_concepts.description: The highest navigable lake in the world is Lake Titicaca (South America). The highest motorable road in the world is now Umling La Pass in Ladakh, India (19,300 feet). The highest polling station in the world is Tashigang in Himachal Pradesh.

important_entities.name: National Highway 44 (NH-44)
important_entities.significance: Runs from Srinagar in the north to Kanyakumari in the south, covering over 3,745 km.

important_entities.name: Vivek Express
important_entities.significance: Runs from Dibrugarh (Assam) to Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu), covering the longest distance and time on the Indian Railway network.

important_entities.name: Statue of Unity
important_entities.significance: Located on the Narmada River in Gujarat, this statue of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel stands at a towering 182 meters.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Older books list the Bandra-Worli Sea Link or Mahatma Gandhi Setu. Currently, the longest 'river bridge' is the Bhupen Hazarika Setu (Assam). However, the recently inaugurated Atal Setu (MTHL - 21.8 km) in Mumbai is now India's longest 'sea bridge' and longest bridge overall. Read the question's phrasing carefully.

If asked for the longest 'Highway' tunnel above 10,000 ft, it is the Atal Tunnel. If asked for the longest road tunnel in India regardless of altitude, it is the Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Tunnel (Chenani-Nashri Tunnel, 9.28 km).

exam_strategy_tips: Current affairs frequently overwrite static infrastructure facts (new bridges, statues, tunnels). In higher-tier exams, examiners deliberately test whether you know the latest inaugurations (like Atal Setu or Umling La) over the legacy facts.
